subject: Contract rollback protection — amendment request and approvals
messages:
From: Julia Conrad <julia.conrad@acmetx.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmetx.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: downsell protections + opt-out language for RD-43291

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are moving toward a pilot commit but procurement has flagged two items they need in the agreement before legal will sign: (1) a clear ramp schedule that lets us reduce committed capacity during the first 6 months without punitive penalties, and (2) a narrowly scoped early-termination / opt-out clause that provides a credit if we downsize the committed tier within the ramp window.

High-level asks from Acme procurement:
- 90-day ramp where we can step down committed units by up to 40% with a negotiated credit (not a full refund)
- If we opt out before month 6, a capped termination credit (proposed by Acme: 25% of unused committed spend)
- Evidence of how this impacts Redwood’s forecasting / capacity so procurement can evaluate risk

Can your team propose specific language and a dollar cap we can circulate with legal? We need a slightly aggressive timeline — our CFO wants this signed by Dec 6 to align with internal budgets.

Attaching our procurement template for reference.

Thanks,
Julia Conrad
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Therapeutics

Attachment: Acme_Procurement_Template.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: downsell protections + opt-out language for RD-43291

Team — forwarding Acme’s ask. TL;DR: they want a 90-day ramp, ability to downsize up to 40% during that window, and an early opt-out credit (~25% proposed). They need language/limits to share with their legal by Dec 2.

Proposed commercial response for deal desk approval:
- Ramp window: 90 days from contract start
- Allowed downsell: up to 40% of committed units within ramp window, in one downsize event
- Early termination / downsize credit: 20% credit on unused committed spend, capped at $50,000
- Condition: credit only applies if customer requests reduction in writing at least 30 days prior to the effective downsize date; no credit for reductions resulting from non-payment or breach
- Operational note: we’ll reserve capacity for the ramp window; finance should confirm impact on revenue recognition

Attachments I’m sending for legal redline: AMENDMENT_Acme_Downgrade_Clause.docx; SOW_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx

Asking for quick approval: Ben (commercial), Karthik (legal), Lauren (final exec approval). If we can sign off on the 20% / $50k cap we can share with Acme and push for Dec 6 signature.

Best,
Soojin
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: AMENDMENT_Acme_Downgrade_Clause.docx (docx stub), SOW_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: downsell protections + opt-out language for RD-43291

Soojin — I support the proposed terms with one tweak: reduce the credit to 15% to preserve economics, but keep the $50k cap. A 20% credit feels generous for a first-year pilot. 15% / $50k should be a reasonable middle ground and still gets us across the line.

Operational asks for visibility: finance should confirm the P&L treatment and we should add a clause that any downsell request during the ramp counts as a one-time election (no repeated step-downs).

Ben
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: downsell protections + opt-out language for RD-43291

Quick legal redline thoughts after looking at the draft amendment:
- Approve the ramp window and one-time downsell election.
- For the termination/downsizing credit, set a cap of $50,000 and limit to 15-20% (recommend 15% to align with Ben).
- Add a clause that the credit is applied as a one-time invoice credit to future invoices; do not treat as cash refund to preserve revenue recognition and simplify bookkeeping.
- Require a written notice 30 days prior and an attestation that the reduction is not due to Redwood breach.
- Add a fallback that if capacity planning is materially impacted (more than two similar downgrades across our customer base in a quarter), Redwood reserves right to renegotiate for future terms.

I’ve attached a marked-up amendment for review. Finance loop (cc'd) to confirm accounting; if finance signs off on credit as invoice credit we can accept 15% / $50k.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel (Commercial Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: AMENDMENT_Acme_Downgrade_Clause.docx (redline stub)

Approved with final parameters:
- Ramp window: 90 days from start
- Single allowed downsell event up to 40% within ramp window
- Early termination / downsell credit: 15% of unused committed spend, capped at $50,000
- Credit applied as invoice credit (no cash refunds)
- Notice: written request 30 days prior; reduction not permitted for reasons of non-payment or material breach
- Operational guardrail: clause allowing Redwood to revisit terms if multiple similar downsizes materially impact capacity forecasting

Soojin — you have executive approval. Get the redlined amendment from Karthik in DocuSign and send to Acme with the SOW ramp schedule. Ask them to countersign by Dec 6 and copy procurement.

Lauren Bishop
